description: GradeThread is an AI-powered SaaS platform providing standardized condition grading for pre-owned clothing. Sellers submit structured photos of garments and receive a numerical condition grade (CG 1.0-10.0), a detailed condition report, and a shareable grade certificate. The platform addresses the trust gap in the $350B+ secondhand clothing market. Tech stack: React 19 + TypeScript + Vite frontend, self-hosted Supabase (api.gradethread.com) for auth/DB/storage, Deno/Hono edge functions for backend API, Claude Vision AI for grading, Stripe for payments, Cloudflare Pages for hosting. Brand colors: Navy #0F3460, Red #E94560, Night #1A1A2E, Soft Gray #F5F5F5. Tailwind v4 + shadcn/ui (New York style). The platform includes full inventory management with financial tracking from acquisition through sale and shipment, detailed financial reporting and analytics, and a comprehensive admin panel for user management, traffic monitoring, and AI model self-refinement.

acceptanceCriteria: Apply to eBay for the restricted sell.negotiation (and commerce.identity.readonly) scopes on the prod keyset.
Once granted, re-add the scope lines and force a re-consent flow at /oauth/start; surface 'reconnect required' to connected sellers.

userStories.notes: [PRE-LAUNCH AUDIT 2026-06-30 · HIGH · ebay · ebay coverage audit] Evidence: services/edge-functions/src/lib/ebay-client.ts:202-204,3258,3330; https://developer.ebay.com/api-docs/sell/negotiation/overview.html [CODE SLICE COMPLETE 2026-07-03 - AC1 (the eBay application itself) remains the USER'S ops step] AC3's code shipped: MIGRATION 00345 (HELD) adds marketplace_connections.negotiation_access_denied mirroring analytics_access_denied; flipdesk-ebay sets it on a /sell/negotiation 403 (tenant-scoped update, best-effort so the 501 always reaches the client) and clears it on any successful eligible/send-offer call. NEW distinction the audit wanted: negotiationScope403Body(deploymentHasScope) - when the deployment DOES request the scope but this token 403s (consented pre-grant), the client gets 501 code=reconnect_required with copy naming the fix ('reconnect your eBay account'), vs the existing feature_unavailable dead-end when the deployment lacks the scope entirely. iOS: EdgeAPIError maps reconnect_required onto featureUnavailable(detail:) (detail carries the server copy); NegotiationStore.EligibleCheck.unavailable now carries detail; the send-offer sheet prefers the server copy - sellers see the reconnect instruction, not an indefinite wait. 2 new edge tests (body pick both ways); full edge 2544/0. AC2's scope lines remain documented ready-to-re-add at getScopes (US-1510). REMAINING: user applies to eBay for sell.negotiation + commerce.identity.readonly on the prod keyset; once granted, re-add the two scope lines and sellers re-consent - the runtime flag + reconnect flow shipped here handles the transition automatically.

userStories.title: EPIC: Buyer Platform — buyer accounts, subscription, and the confidence layer
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want to extend the seller-focused product into a two-sided buyer/seller platform whose sole purpose is increasing confidence in item listings, so that buyers pay a recurring subscription for point-of-purchase confidence AND their demand for graded items pulls more sellers into paying for grading (a two-sided flywheel).
acceptanceCriteria: A buyer can sign up, create a buyer profile, and subscribe to a buyer plan independent of any seller/FlipDesk plan, on the existing Supabase-auth + Stripe stack

The buyer subscription (Free / Guard / Connoisseur) gates a coherent suite of confidence features: extension second-opinion + discrepancy + price-fairness, condition-based alerts, fit, authenticity/video credits, grade-confirmation rewards, buyer trust score, insured grade-locked guarantee, wardrobe portfolio, and the graded-wanted board

Every buyer feature reuses (does not duplicate) an existing capability where one exists — extension US-1753, fit US-1776/1777, authenticity US-1767, video US-1762, circularity US-1785, What's-It-Worth US-1750, badges US-1758, Value Index US-1745, buyer guarantee US-867/guarantee_remedies — and is bound to the buyer entitlement layer
This umbrella tracks the US-1795…US-1847 buyer-platform backlog and its cross-cutting decisions (entitlements, tenant isolation, PII/consent, analytics)
userStories.notes: [P2][BUYER][EPIC][NEW] BASELINE: buyers today are non-account holders reached only via public certificate/verify/guarantee/passport pages; there is NO buyer account, buyer profile, or buyer subscription. All existing plans (FLIPDESK_PLANS, GRADETHREAD_TIERS, CREDIT_PACKS in src/lib/constants.ts) gate seller/reseller capability. STRATEGY: the unique asset is objective per-item condition data + the grade_outcomes dataset (condition->realized price); the buyer product monetizes 'claimed condition vs objective condition, at the point of purchase'. TIERS (confirmed): Free / Guard (~$8/mo) / Connoisseur (~$19/mo). FLYWHEEL: buyer demand for graded items -> sellers must grade to sell -> more graded inventory -> better buyer product. TIES: reuses capability EPICs US-1745/1750/1753/1758/1762/1767/1776/1785 + buyer guarantee US-867. SEQUENCING: foundation (US-1795 sub-epic) ships first; idea sub-epics (US-1805+) depend on it. Child sub-epics: account+subscription foundation (1795), alerts (1805), grade-confirm rewards (1810), buyer trust score (1815), insured grade-locked guarantee (1819), wardrobe portfolio (1824), graded-wanted board (1829), extension confidence suite (1833), buyer bindings for existing capability epics (1839-1844), cross-cutting analytics/legal/QA (1845-1847).

userStories.title: EPIC: GradeThread Rewards — gamified grade -> share -> reward viral loop
userStories.description: As a user, I want to earn points, levels, badges, streaks and real rewards for grading items, completing activities, and sharing my finds so that engagement is fun and habit-forming — and as GradeThread I want the built-in loop (grade -> auto-generated share overlay -> social share -> reward -> public showcase -> new signups) to be our primary viral growth engine.
acceptanceCriteria: A rewards system supports BOTH cosmetic rewards (XP, levels, badges/medals, streaks, leaderboard rank, profile/overlay flair — free and unlimited) AND tangible rewards (free grade credits, subscription discounts, discounted grading — budget-capped and anti-abuse-gated)

The core loop is frictionless: grade an item -> get an auto-generated shareable overlay card -> share it -> the share (and verified click-throughs) earn rewards -> the find can appear in a public showcase feed
All reward earning is event-sourced, idempotent, fraud-resistant, and tangible-reward payout is capped to protect unit-economics margins with an admin kill-switch
userStories.notes: [P2][GAME][EPIC] BASELINE (rails already built to reward ON): grade credits via grant_grade_credits RPC + grade_credit_transactions; referral_milestone_grants (reward-on-threshold precedent); referral_campaign_codes -> immediate credits (redemption model to mirror); Stripe billing in payments.ts; share renderer cert-image-render.ts + SLAB_FORMATS + cert-share-actions.tsx (referral-baked share); cert view/click tracking (content-public.ts /view ?s=) + affiliate_clicks/referral_events attribution; leaderboard opt-in (referrals.ts, referral-leaderboard.tsx) + verified directory. GAP (greenfield): no XP/points, levels, badges/achievements, streaks, quests, showcase feed, or redemption-of-XP-for-rewards. TECH/3P: none new (all in-stack: Postgres event ledger, Stripe coupons, existing renderer). TIES: EPIC 9 (US-1781/1782 auto grade-reveal cards) is the share engine this loop rides; referral/affiliate for attribution; verified directory for leaderboards; unit-economics (Pro 750 / Business 2000 AI-action caps, 40% margin floor) constrains tangible rewards; admin-fraud/admin-safety for anti-gaming; notifications/drip for re-engagement; feature_flags for kill-switch. BUYER: showcase feed to browse cool finds (SEO + social). SELLER/USER: fun, status, streaks, real discounts, effortless sharing. ECONOMICS RULE: cosmetic rewards unlimited; tangible rewards MUST be capped + fraud-gated + margin-aware. Child stories: points engine, achievements, levels/streaks, quests, tangible redemption, share-to-earn, showcase feed, leaderboards, rewards UI, economics/anti-abuse, re-engagement.

userStories.title: Rewards: event-sourced XP/points engine

userStories.title: Rewards: levels, seasons & buyer-side streaks
userStories.description: As a user, I want to level up through seasons of activity so that regular engagement is rewarding — without a streak mechanic that punishes the bursty, seasonal rhythm of reselling.
acceptanceCriteria: XP thresholds map to named levels/tiers (e.g. Thrifter -> Picker -> Curator -> Archivist -> Legend) shown as progress toward the next level; level is derived from user_reward_state.xp_total and NEVER decreases

Seller-side activity uses quarterly SEASONS (a season track with goals + season-end recap/rewards that resets cleanly) instead of weekly streaks — a slow sourcing month never destroys accumulated status; recency competition lives on the weekly leaderboards (US-1856), not on identity

Calendar streaks exist only where a genuinely daily/weekly surface exists — the buyer extension + confirmation flow (US-1814) — with grace/streak-freeze rules; seller surfaces show season progress instead
Levels unlock cosmetic perks (profile flair, exclusive share-card frames/overlays) with no hard paywall
userStories.notes: [P2][GAME] Level thresholds + season logic in a rewards lib; season rollover timezone-aware (reuse scheduled-drops tz handling). Cosmetic overlay frames = additional cert-image-render templates gated by level. No tangible cost = unlimited. Refined 2026-07-09: streaks are the wrong loyalty primitive for bursty resellers — replaced with seasons; streaks kept buyer-side only. Tenure/loyalty tiers split out to US-1914.

userStories.title: Rewards: quests & time-boxed challenges (personal + community)

Time-boxed community/seasonal challenges (e.g. 'Best thrift find of the month') that can feed the showcase feed and leaderboards
Admin-configurable quest definitions (criteria, window, reward) with start/end and a kill-switch
userStories.notes: [P2][GAME] Migration triple for quests (config, deny-all) + user_quest_progress (tenant RLS). Progress derived from reward_events. Community challenges tie to the showcase feed + leaderboards. Admin CRUD via a new admin surface (mirror admin-growth patterns).

userStories.title: Rewards: milestone-granted tangible rewards (credits + discounts) — XP is never spent
userStories.description: As a user, I want crossing XP/badge milestones to GRANT me real perks (free grade credits, subscription/grading discounts) so that engagement pays off — without spending XP, so my level and leaderboard rank never go backwards for redeeming.
acceptanceCriteria: XP is permanent and only ever accrues (status currency: levels, leaderboards); tangible value is granted when crossing configured milestones — XP is NEVER debited. Spendable currency is the existing grade-credit ledger, not XP

A milestone-rewards catalog (reward_type free_grade_credits | subscription_discount | per_grade_discount, trigger = XP threshold | badge | season goal, value, monthly + lifetime caps) that admins configure

Granting free grade credits reuses grant_grade_credits into grade_credit_transactions; subscription discounts issue a Stripe coupon/promo applied in payments.ts; per-grade discounts apply at the payment-precedence step
Every grant is recorded in a redemption/grant ledger, is idempotent per (user, milestone), respects per-user and global caps, and cannot double-issue
userStories.notes: [P2][GAME][BILLING] Migration triple for milestone catalog + user_reward_grants ledger. Credits reuse grant_grade_credits (as referral_campaign_codes already do). Stripe coupon path in payments.ts (subscribe/downgrade). Per-grade discount hooks runPaymentPrecedence (grade-billing.ts). MUST enforce caps from US-1858. Refined 2026-07-09: spend-XP model replaced with milestone-grant model — spending XP deflates status, penalizes redeemers on leaderboards, and invites hoarding; milestone grants avoid all three.

userStories.title: Rewards: share-to-earn loop (auto overlay -> verified share -> reward)
userStories.description: As a user, I want to be rewarded for sharing my graded finds so that showing off my finds is both fun and worthwhile — the core viral trigger.

A 'Viral Find' badge + escalating rewards for finds that drive N verified click-throughs or a signup
userStories.notes: [P2][GAME][SHARE][GROWTH] Depends on EPIC 9 US-1782 (auto reveal card) + cert-share-actions.tsx referral bake + cert_view ?s= + affiliate_clicks/referral_events. userStories.title: Thrift Radar: aggregation engine + k-anonymity floor
userStories.description: As the Radar system, I need scheduled aggregation that turns anonymized scan events into venue-level intelligence (brand density, grade quality, freshness) that is only ever served above an anonymity floor.
acceptanceCriteria: Scheduled aggregation job (durable-jobs conventions: claim/heartbeat/reclaim, cron_runs visibility) computes venue x brand x time-window stats: scan count, distinct-contributor count, average estimated grade, buy-verdict rate, last-activity freshness.

Raw radar_scan_events older than the retention window are rolled up and pruned; retention is configurable.
Read-only edge endpoint serves aggregates (venue list by bounding box + venue detail); responses contain no per-user or per-contributor data.
deno tests cover the aggregation math, k-floor enforcement, and retention pruning; migration follows the US-1108 triple.

userStories.title: Lister reliability: job state must survive MV3 service-worker death
userStories.description: As a seller, I want a cross-post job to complete even when the marketplace page loads slowly, so jobs stop silently vanishing. Audit: ALL job state (jobsByTab, pendingExternal) is in-memory in the SW (extension/background.js:25-27); Chrome kills an idle SW ~30s after the last event and an open sendResponse channel does NOT keep it alive (the code's keep-alive comment at background.js:23-24 is factually wrong); safety timeouts use setTimeout which dies with the SW (background.js:144-157,190-203).
acceptanceCriteria: Job state persists in chrome.storage.session keyed by tabId + jobId; a freshly-restarted SW serves GT_LISTER_GET_JOB from storage, so a fill still runs after SW suspension
Job timeouts use chrome.alarms (not setTimeout) driven off persisted job state; on alarm, the job is failed, storage cleaned, and the SaaS informed

Result delivery no longer relies on the original sendResponse surviving SW death: the extension messages the originating GradeThread tab (tabId persisted with the job) with the result, and the frontend bridge (src/lib/lister-extension.ts) listens for that push in addition to the callback

Tab-close cleans BOTH the job entry and the pending SaaS response (immediate 'tab was closed' error instead of the 130s timeout); a fill completing after timeout is reported as late-success rather than silently dropped
handleListRequest/handleDelistRequest wrap their async bodies so a storage throw still calls sendResponse with an error (no unhandled-rejection hangs)
userStories.notes: Audit findings F1/F2/F3/F10/F11/F12 (critical cluster). This is the top correctness fix for the seller surface.

userStories.title: Lister delist correctness + login-wall detection
userStories.description: As a seller who sold elsewhere, I want extension delist to actually work and to never claim success falsely, and I want a login wall diagnosed as 'log in and retry' instead of 'selectors broke'. Audit: the Poshmark delist probe requires the remove control to exist BEFORE the menu opens (extension/content/common.js:192-219 + selectors.js:44) so the shipped-enabled flow can basically never pass probe; when it does run, it reports delisted:true without verifying deletion (common.js:220-225); a login redirect consumes the job and mis-reports selector breakage (poshmark.js + background.js:234).
acceptanceCriteria: Delist probe validates in interaction order: probe menu → click menu → wait for remove control → click → wait for confirm; required-selector sets reflect what can exist pre-interaction

Success is reported ONLY after verifying the deletion took effect (navigation away / listing-gone / marketplace confirmation toast); anything less returns ok:false with a 'verify manually' message — the pending-delist queue stamp must NOT clear on unverified outcomes (preserves US-1629 double-sale protection)

Content scripts detect marketplace login/interstitial pages (URL + form heuristics) and respond 'log in to <platform> and retry' WITHOUT consuming the job; after the user logs in and lands on the target page, the job still runs
Probe waits for independent selectors run concurrently (Promise.all) so a broken form is diagnosed in ~6s not 18-24s
A tenant-isolation-style test isn't applicable (no server code), but the flows get deterministic DOM fixture tests for probe ordering and delist verification
userStories.notes: Audit findings F5/F6/F7/F18. F6 is the nastiest failure mode in the product: false 'delisted' = item stays live after selling elsewhere.

userStories.title: Lister: capture the real listing URL and stop recording prefills as active listings
userStories.description: As a seller, I want my cross-listing recorded with its real marketplace URL only once it's actually live, so my inventory doesn't show phantom active listings. Audit: GT.captureListingUrl is referenced in a comment but doesn't exist anywhere — listingUrl is always null (extension/content/common.js:168-169) despite the README claiming listing_url is recorded; the frontend writeback (src/components/flipdesk/listing-kit.tsx:476-518 → /api/flipdesk/listings/extension-writeback) marks the listing active + listed_at:now when the form was merely PREFILLED and the seller hasn't clicked List; partial photo attach reports photosAttached:true (common.js:88-96).
acceptanceCriteria: After a fill, the content script watches for the tab navigating to a live-listing URL (per-platform URL pattern in selectors.js) for a bounded window and reports it; the extension pushes a follow-up GT_LISTER_LISTED message with the captured URL to the originating GradeThread tab

Writeback records status 'prefilled' (or listing_status distinct from active) at fill time; it flips to active with listing_url + listed_at only on the follow-up confirmation (or via an explicit 'I published it' affordance in the listing kit for when the window is missed)
Auto-delist eligibility (US-717/US-1629) keys off confirmed-active listings with a listing_url; prefilled-only rows degrade to the manual delist path with honest UI copy
attachPhotos reports per-photo counts (attached/failed) with a per-fetch timeout; partial attach surfaces as 'attached 6 of 8 — drag the rest in' rather than success
Migration for any new listing_status value follows the migrations skill triple; edge writeback stays owner-verified (US-268) with a tenant-isolation test for the new confirm transition

recentReads entries always pair the score with the URL that was actually graded

userStories.title: Cross-browser: Firefox + Edge support for the unified extension

The research surface (condition read) works end-to-end on Firefox: config fetch, grade call (README's moz-extension origin in EXTENSION_ALLOWED_ORIGINS documented in .env.example), overlay, popup, storage — verified manually on a real listing; Firefox's opt-in host-permissions flow is handled (prompt or graceful degradation)

Edge: the unified build loads and passes a manual smoke on Edge; store packaging checklist (Edge Add-ons) appended to US-1757's distribution scope

userStories.title: Public grading endpoint hardening: trusted client IP, DNS-rebinding pin, honest quota errors
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we don't want the extension's public endpoint quota to be bypassable or its errors misattributed. Audit: clientIpFor() in public-grading.ts:185-191 blindly trusts cf-connecting-ip / first XFF hop even in prod — unlike the hardened clientIp() in middleware/rate-limit.ts (US-354) which requires the cf-origin-secret proof — so direct-to-origin callers rotate headers for unlimited per-IP quota (same weakness in /grade-check); safeFetch validates the resolved IP then lets fetch re-resolve (ssrf.ts:226-231), leaving a 0-TTL DNS-rebinding window the file's own header claims is closed; AI-daily-ceiling exhaustion surfaces as 400 'make sure the URL points to a public photo', blaming the user and inviting quota-burning retries.
acceptanceCriteria: public-grading routes resolve the client IP via the hardened clientIp() (cf-origin-secret proof, no raw XFF trust in prod); null IP → 429/400, never unlimited; applied to grade-from-url AND grade-check

safeFetch connects to the IP it validated: resolve once, pin (connect by IP with Host/SNI handling, or re-resolve-and-verify with the fetch's resolution) so validation and connection can't diverge; ssrf tests cover the rebinding scenario

Server-side capacity conditions (AI ceiling, concurrency) return 503 with a distinct machine-readable code; the extension renders 'GradeThread is at capacity, try later' as NON-retryable, distinct from bad-URL 400s
EXTENSION_ALLOWED_ORIGINS + the extension-id env story added to services/edge-functions/.env.example and LAUNCH_CHECKLIST.md
Existing quota/SSRF tests extended; per-instance in-memory quota limitation stays documented as accepted until US-1838's authenticated metering
userStories.notes:
Integration audit Medium x2 + Low. Edge-only story (services/edge-functions) — tenant-isolation skill applies to any new endpoint; the durable per-user metering is US-1838, not this. 

PARTIAL 2026-07-15 (agent loop — story stays passes:false). DONE (AC1): closed the production per-IP quota bypass — clientIpFor() in public-grading.ts blindly trusted client-controlled X-Forwarded-For, so a direct-to-origin caller rotated XFF to mint unlimited per-IP free-grade buckets on grade-check/grade-from-url/authenticity-check. Reimplemented clientIpFor() to delegate to the hardened clientIp() (US-354: CF-Connecting-IP only, gated on cf-origin-secret proof); a no-trustworthy-IP request now collapses to ONE shared sentinel bucket (NO_TRUSTWORTHY_IP) — degraded, never unlimited. 3 deno tests added to grade-check_test.ts (XFF-rotation collapses to sentinel; CF-Connecting-IP trusted; forged CF-IP without secret → sentinel). .env.example CF_ORIGIN_SECRET note extended to cover the public grading quota. Verified: deno lint + deno test grade-check_test.ts green (23), deno check public-grading.ts. NOT DONE (blocks passes): AC2 — safeFetch DNS-rebinding socket-pin: assertPublicUrl already resolves+validates ALL A/AAAA records and RETURNS the validated IPs, but safeFetch discards them and lets fetch() re-resolve (the rebinding window). A literal connect-by-validated-IP is not robustly achievable in Deno stable fetch for HTTPS (no SNI/Host/cert override; no custom resolver on Deno.createHttpClient) — needs a design decision (accept all-records validation + immediate re-resolve as the mitigation, or a Deno.connect-based client). AC3 — distinct 503 machine-readable capacity code for AI-ceiling/concurrency (currently misattributed as a bad-URL 400) + extension non-retryable render. AC4 — EXTENSION_ALLOWED_ORIGINS + extension-id env still undocumented (CF_ORIGIN_SECRET portion done). AC5 — SSRF rebinding test still owed with AC2. 

PARTIAL 2026-07-15 (cont.) DONE (AC3): capacity errors now return a distinct machine-readable 503 instead of the misattributed bad-URL 400. quick-grade.ts no longer SWALLOWS AiCeilingError in its per-image loop (it was masked as "Image analysis failed" → 400) — systemic ceiling errors propagate. public-grading.ts grade-check + grade-from-url catch AiCeilingError → 503 atCapacityBody({error, code:"at_capacity", retryable:false}); authenticity-check aligned from 429 to the same 503 shape. Both buyer extensions (extension-condition + extension-unified) thread code/retryable and render code:at_capacity / status 503 as a NON-retryable "GradeThread is at capacity" state (no retry button). Verified: deno test grade-check_test.ts (24) + full edge suite, deno lint, node --check all 4 extension files, node scripts/test-extensions.mjs (7 files). REMAINING for passes: AC2 (safeFetch DNS-rebinding socket-pin — Deno-fetch limitation, needs design decision) + AC2 rebinding test; AC4 EXTENSION_ALLOWED_ORIGINS + extension-id env docs.
